candidates.summary: Multimodal agents commonly generate freeform reasoning before each action. candidates.title: Plan or Retrieve First? A Scale Study of Tool Discovery Architectures
candidates.summary: Tool-augmented LLM agents discover relevant APIs from large registries before planning execution, yet finite context windows prohibit injecting all tool definitions into a single prompt. The dominant approach, which we term Retrieve-then-Plan (RtP), embeds the user query and retrieves similar tools via approximate nearest-neighbor search. We study an alternative Plan-then-Retrieve (PtR) paradigm in which the LLM first generates Abstract Tool Stubs (hypothesized function signatures describing needed capabilities) which then serve as retrieval queries against the registry. candidates.title: Flint Repair Clinic: a browser lab for real game-generation failures
candidates.summary:
We built Flint Repair Clinic at alphaBell to make small code-generation failures easier to inspect.

It is a browser lab with three real failed/repaired game pairs from our public Flint Arcade development traces. The candidates were generated with stock Recursive Flint Q8_0. You can edit the failed HTML, inspect the browser error, reveal the exact recorded repair, play it and download the original case data with source hashes.

One of the failures was a missing start angle:

ctx.arc(GREENHOUSE.x, GREENHOUSE.y, 34, Math.PI * 2);

candidates.title: Cost-Aware Abstention for LLM-Based IT Ticket Classification
candidates.summary: Wrong automatic routing of an IT support ticket can cost more than human triage. We evaluate cost-aware abstention as an offline, cost-conditional readiness assessment: select a routing policy on calibration data under explicit costs, then evaluate that frozen policy once on held-out test data. On a public 47,837-ticket, eight-class corpus, we compare four trained non-LLM classifiers with four large language models under zero- and few-shot prompting. candidates.title: Reliable AI-Assisted Decisions via Selective Auditing
candidates.summary: We consider online monitoring of an AI system that produces a sequence of decisions. At each round, the system outputs a proposed decision together with a confidence score estimating the trustworthiness of the decision. The decision and confidence score need not be produced by the same model: for example, one agent may propose a decision, while a separate verifier agent evaluates it and outputs a correctness or safety score. candidates.title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
candidates.summary: Auditing whether a text-to-image (T2I) model was fine-tuned on a particular image collection is difficult: a model can absorb collection-level visual characteristics without reproducing training images. Proactive dataset-use auditing plants a shared signal in a dataset before release, then later checks whether that signal appears in a suspect model's generated outputs. candidates.title: BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds
candidates.summary: Frontier coding agents are becoming increasingly adept at 3D modeling. Yet, they still face challenges when building objects meant to be assembled in the physical world, often creating invalid assemblies with floating, colliding, or disconnected parts.
